title: Echocardiography-based machine learning models predict 1-, 3- and 5-year mortality
summary: A ResNet on echo videos and a CatBoost model on echo measurements were trained on 3626 patients in Taiwan (6083 echos) and validated on 595 patients in the Alberta HEART cohort in Canada (997 echos). In external validation the ResNet AUROCs were 82%, 82% and 78% for 1, 3 and 5 years, above CatBoost (78%, 73%, 75%) and better than or comparable to the MAGGIC score. Predicted risk correlated with quality-of-life scores; mortality rates differed between cohorts.
ai_technology: ResNet deep learning on echocardiography videos and CatBoost gradient boosting on echo measurements

evidence.unknown: Prospective use for point-of-care risk stratification; effect of different baseline mortality between cohorts; full text not reviewed.
